I checked to see if the runtime was appropriate. Seems about an hour and forty minutes too long.

Twenty minutes in, and it's still awful. I cannot sympathize with Anakin Skywalker. He wasn't a good man seduced by the Dark Side; he was a whiny little prat whose fate surprised no one. His and Padme's romance is unbelievable, as is his "friendship" with Obi-Wan. There is no way to slice up these films and piece together a decent film.

20 minutes is about as far as I could get too. The only reason I knew what was going on was because I had already seen the films and could fill in the pieces. If this was my first viewing of this story, I wouldn't have any idea what was happening, or more importantly, why I should care what's happening. Senator Amidala's life is in jeopardy? Ok, fine. I've only seen her on screen for about 5 minutes. How do I know she's worth saving. I know nothing of her politics or beliefs. For all I know she could be an evil tyrant and it'll probably help her people out if she gets assassinated. You can't just chop out huge sections of a film, or 3 in this case, and expect to maintain the emotional continuity that a coherent film has.

These movies were just exposition for the original trilogy. You can't fix that. All you can do is cut it down so it doesn't take up as much of your time.

Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed the prequels. But I wasn't expecting another trilogy on par with the original, I was just a kid who wanted more Lightsabers and shit.
